topIssues.author: ferranbt

topIssues.title: kona-derive, kona-engine: extension points for custom derivation rules
topIssues.author: ferranbt
topIssues.body:
<!--
Need help?
Refer to our contributing guidelines for additional information about making a good issue:
https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/.github/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md
-->

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
<!--
A clear and concise description of what the problem is. Ex. I'm always frustrated when [...]
-->

We embed kona and need two derivation rules kona does not have, the same way reth lets a node customise its pipeline instead of forking

**Describe the solution you'd like**
<!--
A clear and concise description of what you want to happen.
-->

1. Attach data to a batch. Our batcher submissions carry per-channel data (attestations read from L1 events) that must travel with the batches decoded from that channel down to the attributes. Today `Channel`, `SingleBatch`, `SpanBatch` and `OpAttributesWithParent` have no place for it. An extension slot on attributes (an opaque `Option<Bytes>` or a generic parameter), filled by the data source and carried through the stages untouched, would do.

2. Consolidation policy. `ConsolidateTask` decides whether an unsafe block matches derived attributes. We need to ignore a class of sequencer-injected deposit txs in that comparison and to trigger a reorg from the attached data in (1). A hook on `EngineConfig`, a trait given the attributes and the block, returning match / mismatch, defaulting to today's behaviour.

Both land once for node and proof program since they live in kona-derive and kona-engine. Is this something you would take upstream?

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
<!--
A clear and concise description of any alternative solutions or features you've considered.
-->

Forking kona.

<!--
Add any other context or screenshots about the feature request here.

topIssues.title: kona-node-service: let an embedder drive the sequencer without the admin RPC
topIssues.author: ferranbt
topIssues.body:
<!--
Need help?
Refer to our contributing guidelines for additional information about making a good issue:
https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/.github/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md
-->

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
<!--
A clear and concise description of what the problem is. Ex. I'm always frustrated when [...]
-->

We embed kona-node-service in our own binary, with our own conductor in the same process. After #23881 we can pass the engine provider in. Two things still force an RPC hop to ourselves:
1. `SequencerConfig.conductor_rpc_url` → `RollupNode::start` always builds `ConductorClient::new_http`. `SequencerActor` is already generic over `Conductor`; let the config carry a `Box<dyn Conductor>` instead of a URL.
2. The `SequencerAdminCommand` sender is created in `RollupNode::start` and only given to `AdminRpc`. Expose it to the embedder, e.g. the builder takes the channel or `start` returns a handle. #23491 had this as `SequencerHandle`; just that part would do.

With those two, start/stop/commit/leader stay in-process. `AdminRpc` keeps working as one consumer of the same sender.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
<!--
A clear and concise description of what you want to happen.
-->

Entrypoints in `EngineConfig` to configure the Kona node.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
<!--
A clear and concise description of any alternative solutions or features you've considered.
-->

Connect all the services over JSON-RPC in loopback addresses.

**Additional context**

Add any other context or screenshots about the feature request here.

topIssues.title: contracts-bedrock: dispute game gas and bond sizing under Glamsterdam
topIssues.author: conr2d
topIssues.body:
On Sepolia under Glamsterdam, the receipts of the four dispute game creations I traced show 4.4–4.6 times the gas of a local Osaka replay of the same transactions. The replay (`cast run --quick`) starts from the parent block's state, so the ratio may include a pre-state difference as well as the fork rules. It also does not separate [EIP-8037](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8037) from the other repricings these transactions exercise. EIP-8037 state gas dominates, though: new accounts, code and storage slots make up 86–88% of each receipt's gas.

| Game type | Glamsterdam gas | Osaka gas (replay) |
|---|---:|---:|
| 9 `SuperFaultDisputeGame` | 2,455,999 | 532,891 |
| 1 `PermissionedDisputeGame` | 2,103,594 | 456,482 |
| 42 (Celo) | 1,749,492 | 401,050 |
| 5 `SuperPermissionedDisputeGame` | 1,066,545 | 235,295 |

**Bonds.** The 12 depth-1 `move`s I traced on type 9 games cost 976,066–976,078 gas, against 254,106–254,118 in Osaka replays. The [bond incentives spec](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/blob/main/specs/fault-proof/stage-one/bond-incentives.md) set the first bond at the Fault Proof Mainnet launch, 400,000 gas at 200 gwei, at "approximately double the cost to respond at the top level". Seven type 9 factories I queried, three on mainnet (OP Mainnet, Unichain, Ink) and four on Sepolia, set the root bond (`initBonds`) to 0.08 ETH, that same 400,000 gas. At 200 gwei, it is 157% of the example response's direct gas fee under Osaka (254,118 gas in replay) and 41% under Glamsterdam (976,078 gas). The bond equals the Glamsterdam response's direct gas fee at an effective 82 gwei. Mainnet dispute game creations over about a day I sampled paid 0.08–8.3 gwei. At 8.3 gwei, the example response's direct gas fee is about a tenth of the bond, so I'm not claiming a shortfall at those prices; the question is the sizing rule.

**One small fix.** `wasRespectedGameTypeWhenCreated` has a slot of its own: slot 9 in `SuperFaultDisputeGame`, slot 10 in `FaultDisputeGame` (and `PermissionedDisputeGame`, which inherits its layout). Slot 0 has room for it in both. With the flag packed there, a game created from the new implementation while its type is respected creates one slot fewer: 97,920 state gas, or 4.0% of the sampled type 9 creation and 4.7% of the type 1. Existing games keep their layout. `SuperPermissionedDisputeGame` already keeps the flag in slot 0. I haven't measured the execution-gas change of a patched build.

**Questions.**
1. Is the L1 cost of dispute game creations and moves under Glamsterdam tracked anywhere? I didn't find it in the bodies of #23015 and #23811, or in the titles of the nine public sub-issues of #20151. One of those, #19380, covers the PreimageOracle's reserved gas.
2. Should the root bond, and possibly the `getRequiredBond` curve, be revisited for Glamsterdam?
3. Would a PR for the packing be welcome?

I can share the traces, the per-transaction data and the scripts.

topIssues.title: kona,op-reth: extend TestForkActivationEVMRules with Karst and system-call contracts
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
Follow-up to #24193. Its [`TestForkActivationEVMRules`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/9d6b43638783d98749785e9d76f0f30a3f5b8cb4/rust/kona/tests/proofs/fork_activation_evm_test.go#L77) activates a fork after genesis, runs probes in a block before and a block after the activation block, and proves those blocks with kona. #24193 restores the rules the deleted op-geth tests checked. Two more rules fit the same framework but go beyond that scope.

These are worth pinning because they live in code that kona and op-reth share (op-revm, alloy-op-evm, upstream revm and alloy-evm). A kona proof catches a divergence between kona and op-reth, but not a mistake both make.

## Karst case

Karst has no case yet.

- **CLZ** (EIP-7939): a status probe like the PUSH0 and TSTORE ones (`PUSH1 1 CLZ`) fails before Karst and succeeds after.
- **MODEXP input bound** (EIP-7823): a call to `0x05` with a base longer than 1024 bytes succeeds before Karst and halts after. kona doesn't accelerate MODEXP, so both sides run the same revm code.

Karst's other Osaka changes (MODEXP and P256VERIFY repricing) change gas, not status or output, so they would need a probe that checks gas. Leave them out unless that is cheap to add.

## System-call contracts at their activation block

- **EIP-4788 beacon roots at Ecotone:** an [upgrade deposit deploys the contract](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/89b4a22c130ef374fd15859bf5137b9a1b65b1da/op-node/rollup/derive/ecotone_upgrade_transactions.go#L130) inside the activation block.
- **EIP-2935 block hash history at Isthmus:** an [upgrade deposit deploys the contract](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/89b4a22c130ef374fd15859bf5137b9a1b65b1da/op-node/rollup/derive/isthmus_upgrade_transactions.go#L175) inside the activation block.

In both cases the system call at the start of each block ([`alloy-op-evm`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/89b4a22c130ef374fd15859bf5137b9a1b65b1da/rust/alloy-op-evm/src/block/mod.rs#L1006-L1008)) finds no code in the activation block, so it must do nothing there and start storing from the next block. That ordering is specific to OP chains; on L1 both contracts exist before their fork. A call through the Invoker in the `after` block, reading the parent beacon root or the parent block hash, would pin it.

🤖 *Co-created with Claude Opus 5.5*

topPRs.title: op-chain-ops: add SDM RPC replay checks to check-lagoon
topPRs.author: nonsense
topPRs.body:
Adds read-only SDM RPC validation through `check-lagoon sdm rpc`, with opt-in checks for existing workflows via `--sdm.check-rpc`. Covers debug/parity replay, call-many, transaction-boundary roots, `traceChain`, JS, OTS, and raw/bad-block diagnostics against canonical receipts and state.

JS runs when available; its explicit disabled-tracer response is skipped unless `--sdm.rpc-js` requires it. OTS calls are skipped unless `--sdm.rpc-ots` is set. Unexpected errors and incorrect results still fail. JSON reports distinguish failures from skips; missing fixtures or optional skips leave `complete: false` without failing otherwise successful checks.

Targeted race tests, vet, custom lint, and the op-geth ratchet pass. Default and explicit-required modes were exercised against premium and stock nodes. This is replay-focused coverage, not every RPC/tracer option. Independent review, full-repository lint, and an end-to-end pass against settled-replay release artifacts remain pending.

topPRs.title: op-reth!: launch the stock node from a launcher crate
topPRs.author: joshklop
topPRs.body:
Builds on #24274 (step 3: op-reth as a library with overrides) and should be reviewed after it; the base branch is that PR's.

reth's launch stack (engine tree, pipeline, RPC registry, network, payload service, ExEx manager) is generic, so it is compiled in whichever crate launches a concrete node. `reth-optimism-node` launched op-reth's own node itself (`launch_node`, and `utils::setup` under `test-utils`), so it compiled the whole stack in the same rustc process as all of op-reth's components. That process ran the 16 GB CI executor out of memory (#20100, #20337, tracking #19935).

This PR moves the only instantiation of op-reth's stock launch into a new crate, `reth-optimism-node-launcher`, modelled on tempo's `node-launcher`: non-generic `launch` / `launch_node` functions that return boxed futures, so callers compile neither the stack nor its `poll` code. The `op-reth` binary, the integration tests that launch op-reth's own node and the `exex-hello-world` example go through it. `reth-optimism-node` no longer launches any concrete node. An embedder's `CustomOpNode` still launches through the generic `LaunchOpNode` in the embedder's crate, as in #24274.

No change for operators: the launch (proof history, Storage V1 warning, state-masking check) is the same code, now compiled in another crate.

### Compile memory

Peak RSS of each rustc process, from `/usr/bin/time -l` through a `RUSTC_WORKSPACE_WRAPPER`, on an M-series Mac (16 cores, 64 GB). Both columns use CI's settings: `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0` (`.circleci/continue/helpers.yml`) and `-j 8` (the 8 vCPUs of `xlarge.gen2`). Base is #24274's head `5d23396728`; after is this PR. These numbers are not comparable with #24274's table: incremental builds use 256 codegen units instead of 16 and peaked several GB lower here.

| command | debug base → after | release base → after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cargo build -p reth-optimism-node --all-features` | 18.7 → **0.74** GB (node lib) | 6.3 → **0.95** GB |
| `cargo test -p reth-optimism-node --all-features --no-run`, largest rustc | 18.6 (node lib) → **14.7** GB (`tests/it`) | 8.1 (`e2e_testsuite`) → 9.4 GB (`e2e_testsuite`) |
| same, summed RSS of concurrent rustc processes (sampled) | ~18.0 → **~14.0** GB | ~15.4 → ~13.9 GB |
| `cargo test -p reth-optimism-node --all-features --doc` | 1.4 → 1.0 GB | 4.8 → 3.0 GB |
| CI's `rust-build`: `cargo build --profile dev --workspace`, rebuilding what depends on `reth-optimism-node`, summed concurrent rustc RSS (sampled) | ~14.7 GB | **~14.4 GB** | |
| `cargo build -p op-reth` | 15.5 (node lib) → 15.7 GB (launcher) | 5.7 → 5.9 GB (`op-reth` bin, thin LTO) |

The other processes of the debug test build after this PR: the launcher 12.0 GB, `e2e_testsuite` 7.7 GB (base: 1.8), `tests/it` 14.7 GB (base: 8.3), the node lib 0.7 GB.

The example matters for `rust-build`, which builds the debug workspace on the 16 GB `xlarge.gen2`. `exex-hello-world` launched op-reth's node itself, at 15.3 GB of rustc. On base it had to wait for `reth-optimism-node`; without the example change it compiled at the same time as the launcher, the summed peak reached ~20 GB, and `rust-build` failed on this PR's first push. Through the launcher it compiles only its Ethereum half (9.3 GB) after the launcher.

What I infer from these:
- The launch stack was almost all of `reth-optimism-node`'s compile memory: the lib alone falls from 18.7 to 0.74 GB.
- The `op-reth` binary build is unchanged, as expected: it compiles the same stack once, in the launcher instead of the node lib.
- In debug, the test binaries got heavier. Debug builds share generic instances across crates, and on base `tests/it` and `e2e_testsuite` reused the copy that `utils::setup` (reth's E2E harness on op-reth's node) had compiled into the lib. Now `tests/it` compiles the three node types of the `custom_pool/` tests itself, and that is its 14.7 GB. Taking the E2E harness out of `tests/it` as well made no difference (14.9 GB), so this PR keeps those tests on the harness.
- Release builds share no generics, so there each test binary compiles its own copies before and after; the 9.4 vs 8.1 GB of `e2e_testsuite` is within the run-to-run noise I saw.

### CI executor

The affected job is `rust-ci-cargo-tests` (`rust-tests` in the `rust-ci` workflow), moved to `2xlarge.gen2` by #20100. It runs `just test`, which since #24192 also runs the doc tests that #20337 had moved to `2xlarge.gen2` in the former `rust-doctest` job. This PR does not make `xlarge.gen2` (16 GB) viable for it: the largest rustc process of its debug build is still `tests/it` at 14.7 GB, and the job compiles the rest of the workspace with up to 8 other rustc processes at the same time. Measured on macOS, not on the CircleCI Linux image. To get there, the `custom_pool/` tests' node types would have to be split across test binaries or launched through `OpNode::with_pool`; I left that for a follow-up. `op-reth-compact-codec` (`xlarge.gen2`, a debug `cargo run --bin op-reth --features dev`) is not helped either: a debug `op-reth` build peaks at 15.5–15.7 GB before and after (measured without `dev`).

### Review

`rust-code-reviewer` and `deletion-reviewer` ran on the diff. Dismissed or deferred:
- Make `launch` take `(builder, node)` like `launch_node`: kept taking a built `OpRethLaunchBuilder`, as tempo does, so a caller can still add hooks such as `extend_rpc_modules` before launching.
- Have the test helper set `num_state_masking_blocks = 0`: the tests launched with reth's default of 30 before this PR too; changing the tested config is out of scope.
- Re-export the launcher from the `reth-op` umbrella crate: not done; nothing uses `reth_op::node::launch_node`.

BREAKING CHANGE: `reth_optimism_node::launch_node` (also reachable as `reth_op::node::launch_node`) moves to `reth_optimism_node_launcher::launch_node`, which takes the same `(builder, node, hooks)` and returns a boxed future. `reth_optimism_node::utils::setup` (`test-utils`) is removed: build the nodes with `E2ETestSetupBuilder::<OpNode>::new(n, utils::chain_spec()).with_attributes_generator(utils::optimism_payload_attributes).build()`. Premium uses neither.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

topPRs.title: contracts-bedrock: add ComplianceModule end-to-end tests
topPRs.author: 0xarktos
topPRs.body:
**Description**

Adds end-to-end Foundry tests that run the Portal, the L1StandardBridge, the L1CrossDomainMessenger, the ComplianceModule and VisionPolicyV1 together. The module is deployed and set as the Portal's bridge hook through a real OPCM upgrade, and VisionPolicyV1 makes every screening decision.

A shared `ComplianceIntegration_TestInit` deploys the system and provides helpers to deposit through the real entry points, read held deposits and withdrawals back from the module's `Held` event, build and prove withdrawals, and assert custody on the Portal, the bridge and the module.

**Tests**

30 integration tests in `test/integration`, gated on `DEV_FEATURE__BRIDGE_HOOK`:

- Deposits and withdrawals of ETH, escrowed ERC20, mintable ERC20 and zero-value messages run through hold, clearance and completion. Each held item is compared with the same item proceeding directly: a deposit must publish an identical `TransactionDeposited`, and a withdrawal must make an identical call with the same `l2Sender` (FM5).
- A deposit from a contract is held and completed with its aliased sender, while the policy screens the contract's own address.
- Every completed deposit is checked against the terms of its held item, so a completion cannot publish a different sender, target, value, gas limit or data.
- `clearAndCompleteDeposit` and `clearAndCompleteWithdrawal` run through `multicall`. One entry that cannot complete reverts the whole batch, and the other entry completes when the batch is sent again without it (Policy FM5).
- Failures and retries: a reverting withdrawal target, a failed messenger relay replayed later, a completion over the block's deposit gas limit, duplicate completions, and revoked or expired verdicts. Each checks balances, escrow and held records.
- Policy outcomes seen through the Portal: rejection before the hold delay, immediate holds for denied parties and expired verdicts, the Fee Vault rule, and the pause.
- Hook lifecycle: deployment wiring and ownership, disable with a nonce cutoff and re-enable, and hook removal followed by setting the same module again and completing the items held before (FM18).
- Upgrades: an OPCM upgrade, a module upgrade and a policy swap each keep held funds, verdicts and records, and the held items complete afterward on their held terms.

**Additional context**

- Devnet tests, op-deployer flows and resuming interrupted deployments are not part of this PR.
- The tests deploy the module and policy inline.
- Deposits are asserted up to the `TransactionDeposited` event on L1. L2 execution is left to the devnet tests.
- The test deployment respects a game type that its OPCM config does not enable, so the upgrade helper overrides the respected game type for the upgrade and restores it afterward.
- The tests run in the `BRIDGE_HOOK` entry of the CI dev-feature matrix and skip elsewhere, because OPCM rejects a bridge hook while the feature is off.

**Metadata**

Closes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism-private/issues/746

topPRs.title: ci(images): add opt-in -slim variants for all images
topPRs.author: falcorocks
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Every image in the catalog gets an additional `-slim` variant, built from a dedicated `apko/<image>-slim.yaml` that omits `apk-tools` and `busybox`. Where an image's binaries do not link libssl or libcrypto, the slim variant also omits `openssl` and `ca-certificates`. `ca-certificates-bundle` is kept in every variant.

Canonical tags are unchanged. Both variants of each image are planned and smoke tested with the image's existing smoke commands, none of which need a shell.

Stacked on #24404.
